answer: An agent economy can require each identity to keep a live 4-gigabyte opal working set in memory, refreshed by a whisper challenge naming a random slice every few minutes. A verifier checks the slice hash against that identity's registered commitment, and a wrong or missing slice is public proof the set was not live. An honest agent holds one set, while an attacker running 1,000 identities must hold 4 terabytes live at once, because one set cannot answer two different whisper challenges at the same time. A lotus registry records each commitment once, so a shared set fails both checks.
